title: paged KV cache: eviction/pinning reuse optimizations
author: Ava Nguyen
description: Motivation: Reduce tail latency and memory churn in the paged KV cache under mixed workload patterns by improving block allocator reuse, pinning semantics, and eviction heuristics. This PR consolidates multiple allocator codepaths, adds locality-aware pinning heuristics, and exposes a conservative reuse policy that reduces allocation churn for bursty prefix-heavy workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Refactor block allocator to expose a reusable free-list with fast-path for same-size block reuse and per-GPU locality buckets; 2) Introduce pinning tokens for actively-used KV ranges with TTL-based heuristics and explicit elevated-priority pinning for in-flight generations; 3) Replace the global LRU eviction scan with a two-tier eviction (locality-first, then age) to avoid evicting blocks needed by co-located requests; 4) Add metrics and tracing points for allocation hits/misses, pin hits, eviction decisions, and per-bucket utilization; 5) Add integration tests and a perf-canary harness that reproduces prefix-heavy chat workloads. Backwards compatibility: runtime API unchanged; config knobs added under kv_cache.{reuse_policy,pinning_ttl,locality_buckets} with safe defaults. Rollout: Gradual canary on Dedicated and Hosted with feature gated flags; fallback to previous allocator on regressions. Related: Linear ENG-1423 (KV cache eviction failures under bursts), ENG-1439 (sched + cache interplay).

release_notes: Improves paged KV cache allocation and eviction: reduces allocation churn and tail latency for prefix-heavy workloads, adds locality-aware pinning and reuse policy. Config knobs: kv_cache.reuse_policy, kv_cache.pinning_ttl. No API-breaking changes.
perf_benchmarks: Microbench (alloc hot-path): reuse hit rate improved from 42% -> 78% on steady-state prefix traffic
End-to-end canary (prefix-heavy chat): 95th latency reduced by ~12% and p99 reduced by ~18% at 95th percentile concurrency
Throughput: sustained throughput improved by ~6% in Dedicated 4xA100 cluster under mixed workload due to fewer evictions and re-populates
testing: Unit tests for allocator concurrency and free-list correctness
Integration test reproducing prefix-heavy chat workload and validating no KV corruption
Perf-canary run across dedicated clusters comparing baseline and new allocator
